verses.displayText: Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven.
verses.context: Right after the light comparison, Jesus tells the crowd why that light matters: so people notice good actions and credit God.

verses.text: But I say unto you, That ye resist not evil: but whosoever shall smite thee on thy right cheek, turn to him the other also.
verses.displayText: But I say unto you, That ye resist not evil: but whosoever shall smite thee on thy right cheek, turn to him the other also.
verses.context: Addressing an old rule about fair payback, Jesus tells his listeners to respond to a slap by not retaliating at all.

verses.text: After this manner therefore pray ye: Our Father which art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name.
verses.displayText: After this manner therefore pray ye: Our Father which art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name.
verses.context: Teaching his disciples how to pray, Jesus gives them this opening line as a model to follow.

verses.text: Give us this day our daily bread.
verses.displayText: Give us this day our daily bread.
verses.context: Continuing the model prayer he gave his disciples, Jesus includes this simple request for each day's needs.

verses.text: And forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors.
verses.displayText: And forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors.
verses.context: The same model prayer continues with a line linking being forgiven to forgiving others.

verses.text: For if ye forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you:
verses.displayText: For if ye forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you:
verses.context: Right after teaching the model prayer, Jesus explains what happens when his listeners forgive other people.

verses.text: For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.
verses.displayText: For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.
verses.context: In a teaching about where to put your effort, Jesus tells the crowd that their heart follows whatever they treasure.

verses.text: Behold the fowls of the air: for they sow not, neither do they reap, nor gather into barns; yet your heavenly Father feedeth them. Are ye not much better than they?
verses.displayText: Behold the fowls of the air: for they sow not, neither do they reap, nor gather into barns; yet your heavenly Father feedeth them. Are ye not much better than they?
verses.context: Pointing to birds flying overhead, Jesus asks his listeners to notice how God feeds them without their working for it.

verses.text: Fear ye not therefore, ye are of more value than many sparrows.
verses.displayText: Fear ye not therefore, ye are of more value than many sparrows.
verses.context: Sending his disciples out to preach, Jesus reassures them of their worth by comparing them to sparrows.

verses.text: But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.
verses.displayText: But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.
verses.context: Still teaching about worry over food and clothing, Jesus tells the crowd what to prioritize instead.

verses.text: Take therefore no thought for the morrow: for the morrow shall take thought for the things of itself. Sufficient unto the day is the evil thereof.
verses.displayText: Take therefore no thought for the morrow: for the morrow shall take thought for the things of itself. Sufficient unto the day is the evil thereof.
verses.context: Closing his teaching on worry, Jesus tells the crowd not to borrow trouble from a day that hasn't come yet.

verses.text: Judge not, that ye be not judged.
verses.displayText: Judge not, that ye be not judged.
verses.context: In a teaching about how people treat each other, Jesus opens with a short warning against judging others.

verses.text: Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you:
verses.displayText: Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you:
verses.context: Continuing to teach the crowd, Jesus encourages them to keep asking, searching, and knocking.

verses.text: Therefore all things whatsoever ye would that men should do to you, do ye even so to them: for this is the law and the prophets.
verses.displayText: Therefore all things whatsoever ye would that men should do to you, do ye even so to them: for this is the law and the prophets.
verses.context: Summarizing a large section of his teaching, Jesus reduces it to one rule about treating others the way you want to be treated.

verses.text: Because strait is the gate, and narrow is the way, which leadeth unto life, and few there be that find it.
verses.displayText: Because strait is the gate, and narrow is the way, which leadeth unto life, and few there be that find it.
verses.context: Describing two possible paths, Jesus tells the crowd that the one leading to life is narrow and less traveled.

verses.text: Therefore whosoever heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them, I will liken him unto a wise man, which built his house upon a rock:
verses.displayText: Therefore whosoever heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them, I will liken him unto a wise man, which built his house upon a rock:
verses.context: Closing the Sermon on the Mount, Jesus compares someone who acts on his words to a builder who chose solid rock.

verses.text: Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.
verses.displayText: Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.
verses.context: Speaking to a crowd worn down by life, Jesus invites anyone tired and burdened to come to him for rest.

verses.text: Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls.
verses.displayText: Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls.
verses.context: Right after that invitation, Jesus describes himself as gentle and humble, offering rest to those who follow him.

verses.text: And immediately Jesus stretched forth his hand, and caught him, and said unto him, O thou of little faith, wherefore didst thou doubt?
verses.displayText: And immediately Jesus stretched forth his hand, and caught him, and said unto him, O thou of little faith, wherefore didst thou doubt?
verses.context: After Peter starts walking on the water toward him and then panics and sinks, Jesus catches him and asks why he doubted.

verses.text: And Jesus said unto them, Because of your unbelief: for verily I say unto you, If ye have faith as a grain of mustard seed, ye shall say unto this mountain, Remove hence to yonder place; and it shall remove; and nothing shall be impossible unto you.
verses.displayText: And Jesus said unto them, Because of your unbelief: for verily I say unto you, If ye have faith as a grain of mustard seed, ye shall say unto this mountain, Remove hence to yonder place; and it shall remove; and nothing shall be impossible unto you.
verses.context: After the disciples fail to heal a boy, Jesus tells them that faith as small as a mustard seed would have been enough.

verses.text: For where two or three are gathered together in my name, there am I in the midst of them.
verses.displayText: For where two or three are gathered together in my name, there am I in the midst of them.
verses.context: Teaching about resolving conflict within a community, Jesus promises his own presence wherever even a small group gathers in his name.

verses.text: Wherefore they are no more twain, but one flesh. What therefore God hath joined together, let not man put asunder.
verses.displayText: Wherefore they are no more twain, but one flesh. What therefore God hath joined together, let not man put asunder.
verses.context: Responding to a question about divorce, Jesus describes marriage as something God joins that people shouldn't split apart.

verses.text: But Jesus said, Suffer little children, and forbid them not, to come unto me: for of such is the kingdom of heaven.
verses.displayText: But Jesus said, Suffer little children, and forbid them not, to come unto me: for of such is the kingdom of heaven.
verses.context: When his disciples try to keep children away from him, Jesus tells them to let the children come instead.

verses.text: But Jesus beheld them, and said unto them, With men this is impossible; but with God all things are possible.
verses.displayText: But Jesus beheld them, and said unto them, With men this is impossible; but with God all things are possible.
verses.context: After his disciples wonder aloud who could possibly be saved, Jesus tells them that what's impossible for people isn't impossible for God.

verses.text: Jesus said unto him, Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind.
verses.displayText: Jesus said unto him, Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind.
verses.context: Asked by a religious lawyer to name the most important commandment, Jesus answers with total love for God.

verses.text: And the King shall answer and say unto them, Verily I say unto you, Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me.
verses.displayText: And the King shall answer and say unto them, Verily I say unto you, Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me.
verses.context: In a story about a king judging the nations, Jesus says that kindness shown to the overlooked counts as kindness shown to him.

verses.text: He is not here: for he is risen, as he said. Come, see the place where the Lord lay.
verses.displayText: He is not here: for he is risen, as he said. Come, see the place where the Lord lay.
verses.context: At the empty tomb on the first Easter morning, an angel tells the frightened women that Jesus is not there because he has risen.

verses.text: Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost:
verses.displayText: Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost:
verses.context: Meeting his disciples on a mountain after his resurrection, Jesus sends them out to teach and baptize people everywhere.

verses.text: Teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you: and, lo, I am with you alway, even unto the end of the world. Amen.
verses.displayText: Teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you: and, lo, I am with you alway, even unto the end of the world. Amen.
verses.context: This closes Matthew's Gospel, with the risen Jesus promising his disciples his ongoing presence until the end of time.

verses.text: And Jesus said unto them, Come ye after me, and I will make you to become fishers of men.
verses.displayText: And Jesus said unto them, Come ye after me, and I will make you to become fishers of men.
verses.context: Walking beside the sea and watching two fishermen at work, Jesus calls them to leave their nets and follow him instead.

verses.text: And he arose, and rebuked the wind, and said unto the sea, Peace, be still. And the wind ceased, and there was a great calm.
verses.displayText: And he arose, and rebuked the wind, and said unto the sea, Peace, be still. And the wind ceased, and there was a great calm.
verses.context: Woken up during a violent storm on the lake, Jesus speaks directly to the wind and waves, and they go still.

verses.text: And he said unto them, Why are ye so fearful? how is it that ye have no faith?
verses.displayText: And he said unto them, Why are ye so fearful? how is it that ye have no faith?
verses.context: Right after calming the storm, Jesus asks his frightened disciples why they still had no faith.

verses.text: As soon as Jesus heard the word that was spoken, he saith unto the ruler of the synagogue, Be not afraid, only believe.
verses.displayText: As soon as Jesus heard the word that was spoken, he saith unto the ruler of the synagogue, Be not afraid, only believe.
verses.context: Just after hearing that a synagogue leader's daughter has died, Jesus tells the grieving father not to be afraid, only to believe.

verses.text: For what shall it profit a man, if he shall gain the whole world, and lose his own soul?
verses.displayText: For what shall it profit a man, if he shall gain the whole world, and lose his own soul?
verses.context: Teaching his disciples about the cost of following him, Jesus asks what good it does to gain everything and lose yourself.

verses.text: And straightway the father of the child cried out, and said with tears, Lord, I believe; help thou mine unbelief.
verses.displayText: And straightway the father of the child cried out, and said with tears, Lord, I believe; help thou mine unbelief.
verses.context: Asked by Jesus whether he believes healing is possible, a desperate father cries out this honest, mixed admission.

verses.text: Therefore I say unto you, What things soever ye desire, when ye pray, believe that ye receive them, and ye shall have them.
verses.displayText: Therefore I say unto you, What things soever ye desire, when ye pray, believe that ye receive them, and ye shall have them.
verses.context: Teaching his disciples about prayer after a fig tree withers, Jesus tells them to pray with real expectation of receiving.

verses.text: And the angel said unto them, Fear not: for, behold, I bring you good tidings of great joy, which shall be to all people.
verses.displayText: And the angel said unto them, Fear not: for, behold, I bring you good tidings of great joy, which shall be to all people.
verses.context: Appearing to shepherds watching their flocks at night, an angel tells them not to be afraid, bringing news of great joy.

verses.text: For unto you is born this day in the city of David a Saviour, which is Christ the Lord.
verses.displayText: For unto you is born this day in the city of David a Saviour, which is Christ the Lord.
verses.context: Right after telling the shepherds not to be afraid, the angel announces that a savior has been born in Bethlehem.

verses.text: Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, good will toward men.
verses.displayText: Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, good will toward men.
verses.context: Following the angel's announcement to the shepherds, a whole host of angels bursts into praise over the newborn child.

verses.text: But love ye your enemies, and do good, and lend, hoping for nothing again; and your reward shall be great, and ye shall be the children of the Highest: for he is kind unto the unthankful and to the evil.
verses.displayText: But love ye your enemies, and do good, and lend, hoping for nothing again; and your reward shall be great, and ye shall be the children of the Highest: for he is kind unto the unthankful and to the evil.
verses.context: Teaching a crowd about loving enemies, Jesus tells them to do good and lend without expecting anything back.

verses.text: Give, and it shall be given unto you; good measure, pressed down, and shaken together, and running over, shall men give into your bosom. For with the same measure that ye mete withal it shall be measured to you again.
verses.displayText: Give, and it shall be given unto you; good measure, pressed down, and shaken together, and running over, shall men give into your bosom. For with the same measure that ye mete withal it shall be measured to you again.
verses.context: Continuing to teach about generosity, Jesus tells the crowd that what they give will come back to them in full measure.

verses.text: And he said to them all, If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross daily, and follow me.
verses.displayText: And he said to them all, If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross daily, and follow me.
verses.context: After Peter recognizes him as the Messiah, Jesus tells his disciples what following him will actually require of them daily.

verses.text: But even the very hairs of your head are all numbered. Fear not therefore: ye are of more value than many sparrows.
verses.displayText: But even the very hairs of your head are all numbered. Fear not therefore: ye are of more value than many sparrows.
verses.context: Reassuring his followers not to fear those who could harm them, Jesus points out that even their hairs are counted.

verses.text: I say unto you, that likewise joy shall be in heaven over one sinner that repenteth, more than over ninety and nine just persons, which need no repentance.
verses.displayText: I say unto you, that likewise joy shall be in heaven over one sinner that repenteth, more than over ninety and nine just persons, which need no repentance.
verses.context: Ending a short story about a shepherd finding one lost sheep, Jesus describes the joy in heaven over one person who changes course.

verses.text: And he arose, and came to his father. But when he was yet a great way off, his father saw him, and had compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him.
verses.displayText: And he arose, and came to his father. But when he was yet a great way off, his father saw him, and had compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him.
verses.context: In a story about a runaway son who finally heads home, Jesus describes the father spotting him from far off and running to meet him.

verses.text: For this my son was dead, and is alive again; he was lost, and is found. And they began to be merry.
verses.displayText: For this my son was dead, and is alive again; he was lost, and is found. And they began to be merry.
verses.context: Still telling the same story, Jesus has the father explain the celebration: a son thought dead has come back alive.

verses.text: For the Son of man is come to seek and to save that which was lost.
verses.displayText: For the Son of man is come to seek and to save that which was lost.
verses.context: After spending time in the home of Zacchaeus, a wealthy tax collector, Jesus explains why he came to a man his neighbors despised.

verses.text: Saying, Father, if thou be willing, remove this cup from me: nevertheless not my will, but thine, be done.
verses.displayText: Saying, Father, if thou be willing, remove this cup from me: nevertheless not my will, but thine, be done.
verses.context: Praying alone on the Mount of Olives hours before his arrest, Jesus asks to be spared what's coming, but yields to God's will.

verses.text: Then said Jesus, Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do. And they parted his raiment, and cast lots.
verses.displayText: Then said Jesus, Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do. And they parted his raiment, and cast lots.
verses.context: Nailed to the cross between two criminals, Jesus asks God to forgive the people carrying out his execution.

verses.text: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.
verses.displayText: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.
verses.context: Opening his account of Jesus with poetic language rather than a birth story, John identifies Jesus as 'the Word,' present with God from the very beginning.

verses.text: And the light shineth in darkness; and the darkness comprehended it not.
verses.displayText: And the light shineth in darkness; and the darkness comprehended it not.
verses.context: Continuing that same opening poem, John describes light entering the dark world and the darkness failing to overcome it.

verses.text: But as many as received him, to them gave he power to become the sons of God, even to them that believe on his name:
verses.displayText: But as many as received him, to them gave he power to become the sons of God, even to them that believe on his name:
verses.context: Still in his prologue, John explains what happens to anyone who actually receives and trusts this Word made known as Jesus.

verses.text: And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, (and we beheld his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father,) full of grace and truth.
verses.displayText: And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, (and we beheld his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father,) full of grace and truth.
verses.context: John closes his opening poem by describing this eternal Word becoming human and living among ordinary people.

verses.text: For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.
verses.displayText: For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.
verses.context: Talking at night with Nicodemus, a religious leader who came to him secretly, Jesus explains why God sent his son into the world.

verses.text: For God sent not his Son into the world to condemn the world; but that the world through him might be saved.
verses.displayText: For God sent not his Son into the world to condemn the world; but that the world through him might be saved.
verses.context: Continuing the same nighttime conversation, Jesus clarifies that his purpose was rescue, not condemnation.

verses.text: And Jesus said unto them, I am the bread of life: he that cometh to me shall never hunger; and he that believeth on me shall never thirst.
verses.displayText: And Jesus said unto them, I am the bread of life: he that cometh to me shall never hunger; and he that believeth on me shall never thirst.
verses.context: After feeding a huge crowd with a few loaves of bread, Jesus tells them the next day that he himself is what truly satisfies.

verses.text: So when they continued asking him, he lifted up himself, and said unto them, He that is without sin among you, let him first cast a stone at her.
verses.displayText: So when they continued asking him, he lifted up himself, and said unto them, He that is without sin among you, let him first cast a stone at her.
verses.context: When religious leaders bring a woman caught in adultery to test him, Jesus responds with a challenge about who is qualified to throw the first stone.

verses.text: Then spake Jesus again unto them, saying, I am the light of the world: he that followeth me shall not walk in darkness, but shall have the light of life.
verses.displayText: Then spake Jesus again unto them, saying, I am the light of the world: he that followeth me shall not walk in darkness, but shall have the light of life.
verses.context: Still teaching in the temple after that encounter, Jesus tells the crowd that following him means walking out of darkness.

verses.text: And ye shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free.
verses.displayText: And ye shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free.
verses.context: Speaking to Jews who had just begun to trust him, Jesus links staying faithful to his teaching with actually being set free.

verses.text: The thief cometh not, but for to steal, and to kill, and to destroy: I am come that they might have life, and that they might have it more abundantly.
verses.displayText: The thief cometh not, but for to steal, and to kill, and to destroy: I am come that they might have life, and that they might have it more abundantly.
verses.context: Describing his purpose using the image of a shepherd and thieves, Jesus contrasts destruction with the full life he came to give.

verses.text: I am the good shepherd: the good shepherd giveth his life for the sheep.
verses.displayText: I am the good shepherd: the good shepherd giveth his life for the sheep.
verses.context: Continuing the shepherd imagery, Jesus describes himself as the shepherd willing to die for the sheep in his care.

verses.text: Jesus said unto her, I am the resurrection, and the life: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live:
verses.displayText: Jesus said unto her, I am the resurrection, and the life: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live:
verses.context: Speaking to Martha, whose brother Lazarus had just died, Jesus tells her that life and resurrection are found in him personally.

verses.text: Jesus wept.
verses.displayText: Jesus wept.
verses.context: Standing at the tomb of his friend Lazarus, surrounded by mourners, Jesus is described in this shortest verse simply weeping.

verses.text: A new commandment I give unto you, That ye love one another; as I have loved you, that ye also love one another.
verses.displayText: A new commandment I give unto you, That ye love one another; as I have loved you, that ye also love one another.
verses.context: During his last meal with his disciples, right after washing their feet, Jesus gives them a new instruction about loving one another.

verses.text: By this shall all men know that ye are my disciples, if ye have love one to another.
verses.displayText: By this shall all men know that ye are my disciples, if ye have love one to another.
verses.context: Right after giving that instruction, Jesus tells his disciples that love for each other is what will identify them to others.

verses.text: Let not your heart be troubled: ye believe in God, believe also in me.
verses.displayText: Let not your heart be troubled: ye believe in God, believe also in me.
verses.context: Still at the same last meal, sensing his disciples' fear about what's coming, Jesus tells them not to let their hearts be troubled.

verses.text: In my Father’s house are many mansions: if it were not so, I would have told you. I go to prepare a place for you.
verses.displayText: In my Father’s house are many mansions: if it were not so, I would have told you. I go to prepare a place for you.
verses.context: Continuing to comfort his disciples before his death, Jesus describes going ahead to prepare a place for them.

verses.text: Jesus saith unto him, I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me.
verses.displayText: Jesus saith unto him, I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me.
verses.context: Answering Thomas's question about how to know the way to the Father, Jesus identifies himself as that way.

verses.text: I will not leave you comfortless: I will come to you.
verses.displayText: I will not leave you comfortless: I will come to you.
verses.context: Still preparing his disciples for his departure, Jesus promises he won't leave them permanently alone.

verses.text: Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you: not as the world giveth, give I unto you. Let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid.
verses.displayText: Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you: not as the world giveth, give I unto you. Let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid.
verses.context: Continuing his farewell to his disciples, Jesus leaves them a kind of peace he says is different from what the world offers.

verses.text: I am the vine, ye are the branches: He that abideth in me, and I in him, the same bringeth forth much fruit: for without me ye can do nothing.
verses.displayText: I am the vine, ye are the branches: He that abideth in me, and I in him, the same bringeth forth much fruit: for without me ye can do nothing.
verses.context: Using a vineyard as a picture, Jesus describes himself as the vine and his followers as branches that depend entirely on him.

verses.text: Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends.
verses.displayText: Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends.
verses.context: Still speaking at the same last meal, Jesus defines the greatest possible love as laying down one's life for friends.

verses.text: And ye now therefore have sorrow: but I will see you again, and your heart shall rejoice, and your joy no man taketh from you.
verses.displayText: And ye now therefore have sorrow: but I will see you again, and your heart shall rejoice, and your joy no man taketh from you.
verses.context: Warning his disciples that grief is coming before he leaves them, Jesus promises a joy afterward that no one will be able to take away.

verses.text: These things I have spoken unto you, that in me ye might have peace. In the world ye shall have tribulation: but be of good cheer; I have overcome the world.
verses.displayText: These things I have spoken unto you, that in me ye might have peace. In the world ye shall have tribulation: but be of good cheer; I have overcome the world.
verses.context: Closing this same farewell conversation, Jesus tells his disciples to expect trouble in the world but take heart because he has already overcome it.

verses.text: When Jesus therefore had received the vinegar, he said, It is finished: and he bowed his head, and gave up the ghost.
verses.displayText: When Jesus therefore had received the vinegar, he said, It is finished: and he bowed his head, and gave up the ghost.
verses.context: Dying on the cross after being given a final drink, Jesus speaks three words before he dies.

verses.text: Then saith he to Thomas, Reach hither thy finger, and behold my hands; and reach hither thy hand, and thrust it into my side: and be not faithless, but believing.
verses.displayText: Then saith he to Thomas, Reach hither thy finger, and behold my hands; and reach hither thy hand, and thrust it into my side: and be not faithless, but believing.
verses.context: Appearing to his disciples eight days after his resurrection, Jesus invites the doubting Thomas to touch his wounds directly.

verses.text: Jesus saith unto him, Thomas, because thou hast seen me, thou hast believed: blessed are they that have not seen, and yet have believed.
verses.displayText: Jesus saith unto him, Thomas, because thou hast seen me, thou hast believed: blessed are they that have not seen, and yet have believed.
verses.context: Right after Thomas finally believes upon seeing him, Jesus adds a blessing for people who will believe without ever seeing him at all.

verses.text: But ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you: and ye shall be witnesses unto me both in Jerusalem, and in all Judea, and in Samaria, and unto the uttermost part of the earth.
verses.displayText: But ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you: and ye shall be witnesses unto me both in Jerusalem, and in all Judea, and in Samaria, and unto the uttermost part of the earth.
verses.context: Just before ascending into the sky, Jesus tells his gathered followers what will happen once the promised Spirit comes upon them.

verses.text: Then Peter said unto them, Repent, and be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins, and ye shall receive the gift of the Holy Ghost.
verses.displayText: Then Peter said unto them, Repent, and be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins, and ye shall receive the gift of the Holy Ghost.
verses.context: After a crowd is cut to the heart by his sermon and asks what to do, Peter answers with instructions about repentance and baptism.

verses.text: Then Peter said, Silver and gold have I none; but such as I have give I thee: In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth rise up and walk.
verses.displayText: Then Peter said, Silver and gold have I none; but such as I have give I thee: In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth rise up and walk.
verses.context: Meeting a man who had been unable to walk his whole life, begging at the temple gate, Peter offers him something other than money.

verses.text: Neither is there salvation in any other: for there is none other name under heaven given among men, whereby we must be saved.
verses.displayText: Neither is there salvation in any other: for there is none other name under heaven given among men, whereby we must be saved.
verses.context: Standing before the Jewish council that had arrested him, Peter insists that the name of Jesus is the only one that can rescue anyone.

verses.text: And they said, Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shalt be saved, and thy house.
verses.displayText: And they said, Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shalt be saved, and thy house.
verses.context: After an earthquake breaks open his prison, a terrified jailer asks Paul and Silas what he must do; this is their answer.

verses.text: For in him we live, and move, and have our being; as certain also of your own poets have said, For we are also his offspring.
verses.displayText: For in him we live, and move, and have our being; as certain also of your own poets have said, For we are also his offspring.
verses.context: Speaking to Greek philosophers in Athens, Paul makes his point by quoting their own poets back to them.

verses.text: I have shewed you all things, how that so labouring ye ought to support the weak, and to remember the words of the Lord Jesus, how he said, It is more blessed to give than to receive.
verses.displayText: I have shewed you all things, how that so labouring ye ought to support the weak, and to remember the words of the Lord Jesus, how he said, It is more blessed to give than to receive.
verses.context: Saying goodbye to leaders of the Ephesian church he doesn't expect to see again, Paul reminds them of something Jesus once said about giving.

verses.text: For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ: for it is the power of God unto salvation to every one that believeth; to the Jew first, and also to the Greek.
verses.displayText: For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ: for it is the power of God unto salvation to every one that believeth; to the Jew first, and also to the Greek.
verses.context: Introducing himself to a church he had never visited, Paul explains in this letter why he isn't embarrassed to preach about Jesus.

verses.text: Therefore being justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ:
verses.displayText: Therefore being justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ:
verses.context: Early in this letter to the Roman church, Paul describes the peace with God that comes through trusting Jesus.

verses.text: But God commendeth his love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.
verses.displayText: But God commendeth his love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.
verses.context: Making his case for God's love, Paul points out that Jesus died for people while they were still doing wrong.

verses.text: For the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.
verses.displayText: For the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.
verses.context: Contrasting two different endings, Paul describes what sin earns against what God gives freely instead.

verses.text: There is therefore now no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit.
verses.displayText: There is therefore now no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit.
verses.context: Opening a chapter about life empowered by God's Spirit, Paul assures believers in Jesus that they are no longer condemned.

verses.text: The Spirit itself beareth witness with our spirit, that we are the children of God:
verses.displayText: The Spirit itself beareth witness with our spirit, that we are the children of God:
verses.context: Continuing to describe life in the Spirit, Paul says that same Spirit confirms to believers that they belong to God's family.

verses.text: For I reckon that the sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared with the glory which shall be revealed in us.
verses.displayText: For I reckon that the sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared with the glory which shall be revealed in us.
verses.context: Comparing present difficulty to future glory, Paul argues that current suffering doesn't measure up to what's coming.

verses.text: Likewise the Spirit also helpeth our infirmities: for we know not what we should pray for as we ought: but the Spirit itself maketh intercession for us with groanings which cannot be uttered.
verses.displayText: Likewise the Spirit also helpeth our infirmities: for we know not what we should pray for as we ought: but the Spirit itself maketh intercession for us with groanings which cannot be uttered.
verses.context: Still writing about the Spirit's help, Paul describes the Spirit praying on believers' behalf when they don't know what to say.

verses.text: And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose.
verses.displayText: And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose.
verses.context: Reassuring a church facing hardship, Paul writes that God works everything together for good for those who love him.

verses.text: What shall we then say to these things? If God be for us, who can be against us?
verses.displayText: What shall we then say to these things? If God be for us, who can be against us?
verses.context: Building toward the climax of this chapter, Paul asks a rhetorical question about who could possibly stand against people God is for.

verses.text: Nay, in all these things we are more than conquerors through him that loved us.
verses.displayText: Nay, in all these things we are more than conquerors through him that loved us.
verses.context: Listing off threats like hardship and danger, Paul concludes that none of it can defeat people loved by God.

verses.text: Nor height, nor depth, nor any other creature, shall be able to separate us from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.
verses.displayText: Nor height, nor depth, nor any other creature, shall be able to separate us from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.
verses.context: Closing this chapter, Paul declares that nothing in creation can cut believers off from God's love found in Jesus.

verses.text: That if thou shalt confess with thy mouth the Lord Jesus, and shalt believe in thine heart that God hath raised him from the dead, thou shalt be saved.
verses.displayText: That if thou shalt confess with thy mouth the Lord Jesus, and shalt believe in thine heart that God hath raised him from the dead, thou shalt be saved.
verses.context: Explaining what it means to trust in Jesus, Paul ties together an honest confession with a genuine belief in the resurrection.

verses.text: For whosoever shall call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved.
verses.displayText: For whosoever shall call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved.
verses.context: Continuing that same explanation, Paul writes that calling on the name of the Lord is open to anyone at all.

verses.text: And be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind, that ye may prove what is that good, and acceptable, and perfect, will of God.
verses.displayText: And be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind, that ye may prove what is that good, and acceptable, and perfect, will of God.
verses.context: Urging the Roman church to live differently from the culture around them, Paul calls for a change starting with how they think.

verses.text: Rejoice with them that do rejoice, and weep with them that weep.
verses.displayText: Rejoice with them that do rejoice, and weep with them that weep.
verses.context: In a list of practical instructions for community life, Paul tells believers to share fully in both celebration and grief.

verses.text: Be not overcome of evil, but overcome evil with good.
verses.displayText: Be not overcome of evil, but overcome evil with good.
verses.context: Closing a passage about responding to enemies without revenge, Paul sums it up as overcoming evil by doing good instead.

verses.text: Love worketh no ill to his neighbour: therefore love is the fulfilling of the law.
verses.displayText: Love worketh no ill to his neighbour: therefore love is the fulfilling of the law.
verses.context: Discussing how believers should treat each other, Paul reduces a list of commandments down to a single principle about love.

verses.text: Now the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, that ye may abound in hope, through the power of the Holy Ghost.
verses.displayText: Now the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, that ye may abound in hope, through the power of the Holy Ghost.
verses.context: Near the close of his letter, Paul prays that the Roman believers would be filled with joy, peace, and hope.

verses.text: But as it is written, Eye hath not seen, nor ear heard, neither have entered into the heart of man, the things which God hath prepared for them that love him.
verses.displayText: But as it is written, Eye hath not seen, nor ear heard, neither have entered into the heart of man, the things which God hath prepared for them that love him.
verses.context: Writing to a divided church in Corinth about wisdom beyond human understanding, Paul quotes a line about things no one has ever seen or imagined.

verses.text: What? know ye not that your body is the temple of the Holy Ghost which is in you, which ye have of God, and ye are not your own?
verses.displayText: What? know ye not that your body is the temple of the Holy Ghost which is in you, which ye have of God, and ye are not your own?
verses.context: Confronting sexual immorality within the Corinthian church, Paul reminds them that their own bodies now house God's Spirit.

verses.text: Know ye not that they which run in a race run all, but one receiveth the prize? So run, that ye may obtain.
verses.displayText: Know ye not that they which run in a race run all, but one receiveth the prize? So run, that ye may obtain.
verses.context: Using the image of a foot race, Paul urges the Corinthian believers to run their own lives with the same focus as an athlete chasing a prize.

verses.text: There hath no temptation taken you but such as is common to man: but God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able; but will with the temptation also make a way to escape, that ye may be able to bear it.
verses.displayText: There hath no temptation taken you but such as is common to man: but God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able; but will with the temptation also make a way to escape, that ye may be able to bear it.
verses.context: Warning the Corinthians against repeating Israel's past mistakes, Paul reassures them that God limits how much hardship they'll face at once.

verses.text: Though I speak with the tongues of men and of angels, and have not charity, I am become as sounding brass, or a tinkling cymbal.
verses.displayText: Though I speak with the tongues of men and of angels, and have not charity, I am become as sounding brass, or a tinkling cymbal.
verses.context: Opening his famous chapter on love, Paul says that even the most impressive spiritual gifts amount to noise without it.

verses.text: Charity never faileth: but whether there be prophecies, they shall fail; whether there be tongues, they shall cease; whether there be knowledge, it shall vanish away.
verses.displayText: Charity never faileth: but whether there be prophecies, they shall fail; whether there be tongues, they shall cease; whether there be knowledge, it shall vanish away.
verses.context: Continuing that same chapter, Paul contrasts love's permanence with the temporary nature of spiritual gifts like prophecy.

verses.text: When I was a child, I spake as a child, I understood as a child, I thought as a child: but when I became a man, I put away childish things.
verses.displayText: When I was a child, I spake as a child, I understood as a child, I thought as a child: but when I became a man, I put away childish things.
verses.context: Still writing about love, Paul compares his own growth from childhood to adulthood as a picture of partial knowledge becoming complete.

verses.text: For now we see through a glass, darkly; but then face to face: now I know in part; but then shall I know even as also I am known.
verses.displayText: For now we see through a glass, darkly; but then face to face: now I know in part; but then shall I know even as also I am known.
verses.context: Near the end of the same chapter, Paul admits that present understanding is like a blurry reflection compared to what's coming.

verses.text: And now abideth faith, hope, charity, these three; but the greatest of these is charity.
verses.displayText: And now abideth faith, hope, charity, these three; but the greatest of these is charity.
verses.context: This closes the chapter on love, with Paul ranking faith, hope, and love together, but naming love as the greatest.

verses.text: O death, where is thy sting? O grave, where is thy victory?
verses.displayText: O death, where is thy sting? O grave, where is thy victory?
verses.context: In a chapter defending the resurrection, Paul taunts death itself, asking where its power has gone.

verses.text: But thanks be to God, which giveth us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.displayText: But thanks be to God, which giveth us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.context: Right after taunting death, Paul thanks God for the victory Jesus provides.

verses.text: Who comforteth us in all our tribulation, that we may be able to comfort them which are in any trouble, by the comfort wherewith we ourselves are comforted of God.
verses.displayText: Who comforteth us in all our tribulation, that we may be able to comfort them which are in any trouble, by the comfort wherewith we ourselves are comforted of God.
verses.context: Opening this letter to a church he'd had a painful history with, Paul explains that God comforts him precisely so he can comfort others.

verses.text: For which cause we faint not; but though our outward man perish, yet the inward man is renewed day by day.
verses.displayText: For which cause we faint not; but though our outward man perish, yet the inward man is renewed day by day.
verses.context: Describing the physical toll of his ministry, Paul contrasts his outward decline with an inward renewal happening at the same time.

verses.text: While we look not at the things which are seen, but at the things which are not seen: for the things which are seen are temporal; but the things which are not seen are eternal.
verses.displayText: While we look not at the things which are seen, but at the things which are not seen: for the things which are seen are temporal; but the things which are not seen are eternal.
verses.context: Continuing that same thought, Paul tells the Corinthians to focus on what can't be seen rather than what's only temporary.

verses.text: (For we walk by faith, not by sight:)
verses.displayText: (For we walk by faith, not by sight:)
verses.context: Explaining how he lives with uncertainty about the future, Paul says his confidence rests on trust rather than on visible proof.

verses.text: Therefore if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature: old things are passed away; behold, all things are become new.
verses.displayText: Therefore if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature: old things are passed away; behold, all things are become new.
verses.context: Describing what changes when someone commits to Christ, Paul says the old identity is gone and something new has begun.

verses.text: Every man according as he purposeth in his heart, so let him give; not grudgingly, or of necessity: for God loveth a cheerful giver.
verses.displayText: Every man according as he purposeth in his heart, so let him give; not grudgingly, or of necessity: for God loveth a cheerful giver.
verses.context: Encouraging the Corinthians to follow through on a promised gift for a struggling church, Paul says God loves a giver who gives gladly.

verses.text: And he said unto me, My grace is sufficient for thee: for my strength is made perfect in weakness. Most gladly therefore will I rather glory in my infirmities, that the power of Christ may rest upon me.
verses.displayText: And he said unto me, My grace is sufficient for thee: for my strength is made perfect in weakness. Most gladly therefore will I rather glory in my infirmities, that the power of Christ may rest upon me.
verses.context: After begging God three times to remove a painful affliction, Paul reports the answer he received about God's strength working through weakness.

verses.text: I am crucified with Christ: nevertheless I live; yet not I, but Christ liveth in me: and the life which I now live in the flesh I live by the faith of the Son of God, who loved me, and gave himself for me.
verses.displayText: I am crucified with Christ: nevertheless I live; yet not I, but Christ liveth in me: and the life which I now live in the flesh I live by the faith of the Son of God, who loved me, and gave himself for me.
verses.context: Defending his gospel of grace to churches being pressured toward old religious rules, Paul describes his old identity as replaced by Christ living in him.

verses.text: There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither bond nor free, there is neither male nor female: for ye are all one in Christ Jesus.
verses.displayText: There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither bond nor free, there is neither male nor female: for ye are all one in Christ Jesus.
verses.context: Arguing that faith in Christ erases old social divisions, Paul lists ethnicity, status, and gender as no longer determining anyone's standing.

verses.text: Wherefore thou art no more a servant, but a son; and if a son, then an heir of God through Christ.
verses.displayText: Wherefore thou art no more a servant, but a son; and if a son, then an heir of God through Christ.
verses.context: Explaining what changes for a believer, Paul contrasts being a slave with being an heir who receives an inheritance.

verses.text: Bear ye one another’s burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ.
verses.displayText: Bear ye one another’s burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ.
verses.context: Instructing the Galatian churches on caring for each other, Paul tells them to help carry what weighs each other down.

verses.text: And let us not be weary in well doing: for in due season we shall reap, if we faint not.
verses.displayText: And let us not be weary in well doing: for in due season we shall reap, if we faint not.
verses.context: Encouraging believers who feel worn out doing good, Paul promises a harvest will come if they don't quit.

verses.text: For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God:
verses.displayText: For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God:
verses.context: Writing likely from prison to a church in Ephesus, Paul explains that their rescue came as a gift, not something they earned.

verses.text: For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus unto good works, which God hath before ordained that we should walk in them.
verses.displayText: For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus unto good works, which God hath before ordained that we should walk in them.
verses.context: Right after describing their rescue as a gift, Paul adds that believers are shaped by God to do good things he already planned.

verses.text: And be ye kind one to another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, even as God for Christ’s sake hath forgiven you.
verses.displayText: And be ye kind one to another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, even as God for Christ’s sake hath forgiven you.
verses.context: Instructing the Ephesian church on how to treat each other, Paul ties their forgiveness of one another to the forgiveness they've received.

verses.text: Finally, my brethren, be strong in the Lord, and in the power of his might.
verses.displayText: Finally, my brethren, be strong in the Lord, and in the power of his might.
verses.context: Opening a passage about spiritual struggle, Paul tells the Ephesian believers to draw their strength from God rather than themselves.

verses.text: Put on the whole armour of God, that ye may be able to stand against the wiles of the devil.
verses.displayText: Put on the whole armour of God, that ye may be able to stand against the wiles of the devil.
verses.context: Continuing the same passage, Paul tells believers to dress in spiritual armor to stand against opposition.

verses.text: Being confident of this very thing, that he which hath begun a good work in you will perform it until the day of Jesus Christ:
verses.displayText: Being confident of this very thing, that he which hath begun a good work in you will perform it until the day of Jesus Christ:
verses.context: Writing warmly to a church that had supported him financially, Paul expresses confidence that the good work started in them will be finished.

verses.text: Let nothing be done through strife or vainglory; but in lowliness of mind let each esteem other better than themselves.
verses.displayText: Let nothing be done through strife or vainglory; but in lowliness of mind let each esteem other better than themselves.
verses.context: Urging unity within the Philippian church, Paul tells them to consider others as more important than themselves.

verses.text: I press toward the mark for the prize of the high calling of God in Christ Jesus.
verses.displayText: I press toward the mark for the prize of the high calling of God in Christ Jesus.
verses.context: Describing his own spiritual pursuit as an ongoing race, Paul says he keeps pressing toward the goal rather than settling.

verses.text: Rejoice in the Lord alway: and again I say, Rejoice.
verses.displayText: Rejoice in the Lord alway: and again I say, Rejoice.
verses.context: Writing from prison to a church that had sent him support, Paul repeats a simple command to rejoice.

verses.text: Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God.
verses.displayText: Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God.
verses.context: Continuing that same letter, Paul tells the Philippians to bring their worries to God in prayer instead of carrying them alone.

verses.text: And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.
verses.displayText: And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.
verses.context: Right after that instruction about prayer, Paul describes a peace that goes beyond ordinary understanding.

verses.text: Finally, brethren, whatsoever things are true, whatsoever things are honest, whatsoever things are just, whatsoever things are pure, whatsoever things are lovely, whatsoever things are of good report; if there be any virtue, and if there be any praise, think on these things.
verses.displayText: Finally, brethren, whatsoever things are true, whatsoever things are honest, whatsoever things are just, whatsoever things are pure, whatsoever things are lovely, whatsoever things are of good report; if there be any virtue, and if there be any praise, think on these things.
verses.context: Closing his practical instructions, Paul gives the Philippians a list of the kinds of things worth thinking about.

verses.text: Not that I speak in respect of want: for I have learned, in whatsoever state I am, therewith to be content.
verses.displayText: Not that I speak in respect of want: for I have learned, in whatsoever state I am, therewith to be content.
verses.context: Thanking the Philippians for a gift while writing from prison, Paul says he has learned to be content regardless of his circumstances.

verses.text: I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me.
verses.displayText: I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me.
verses.context: Continuing to describe his contentment, Paul credits his ability to handle any situation to the strength Christ provides.

verses.text: But my God shall supply all your need according to his riches in glory by Christ Jesus.
verses.displayText: But my God shall supply all your need according to his riches in glory by Christ Jesus.
verses.context: Closing his thanks for their gift, Paul assures the Philippians that God will take care of whatever they need in return.

verses.text: And he is before all things, and by him all things consist.
verses.displayText: And he is before all things, and by him all things consist.
verses.context: Describing who Jesus is to a church facing false teaching, Paul says everything holds together because of him.

verses.text: Set your affection on things above, not on things on the earth.
verses.displayText: Set your affection on things above, not on things on the earth.
verses.context: Encouraging the Colossian church toward a new focus, Paul tells them to set their minds on things above rather than earthly concerns.

verses.text: Forbearing one another, and forgiving one another, if any man have a quarrel against any: even as Christ forgave you, so also do ye.
verses.displayText: Forbearing one another, and forgiving one another, if any man have a quarrel against any: even as Christ forgave you, so also do ye.
verses.context: Instructing the Colossian church on relationships, Paul ties forgiving each other directly to how Christ forgave them.

verses.text: And let the peace of God rule in your hearts, to the which also ye are called in one body; and be ye thankful.
verses.displayText: And let the peace of God rule in your hearts, to the which also ye are called in one body; and be ye thankful.
verses.context: Continuing the same instructions, Paul tells the Colossians to let God's peace govern how they treat each other.

verses.text: And whatsoever ye do in word or deed, do all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God and the Father by him.
verses.displayText: And whatsoever ye do in word or deed, do all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God and the Father by him.
verses.context: Closing a section on everyday conduct, Paul tells the Colossians to do everything they say or do in Jesus's name.

verses.text: But I would not have you to be ignorant, brethren, concerning them which are asleep, that ye sorrow not, even as others which have no hope.
verses.displayText: But I would not have you to be ignorant, brethren, concerning them which are asleep, that ye sorrow not, even as others which have no hope.
verses.context: Comforting a church worried about believers who had already died, Paul writes to correct their grief with genuine hope.

verses.text: For if we believe that Jesus died and rose again, even so them also which sleep in Jesus will God bring with him.
verses.displayText: For if we believe that Jesus died and rose again, even so them also which sleep in Jesus will God bring with him.
verses.context: Continuing that same comfort, Paul ties the resurrection of Jesus directly to the hope for those who have died trusting him.

verses.text: Pray without ceasing.
verses.displayText: Pray without ceasing.
verses.context: In a rapid list of short instructions closing his letter, Paul tells the Thessalonians to keep praying without stopping.

verses.text: In every thing give thanks: for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus concerning you.
verses.displayText: In every thing give thanks: for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus concerning you.
verses.context: Right after that instruction, Paul tells the Thessalonians to give thanks in every situation, not just good ones.

verses.text: But the Lord is faithful, who shall stablish you, and keep you from evil.
verses.displayText: But the Lord is faithful, who shall stablish you, and keep you from evil.
verses.context: Reassuring a church worried about difficult people around them, Paul says God is faithful to strengthen and protect them.

verses.text: Now the Lord of peace himself give you peace always by all means. The Lord be with you all.
verses.displayText: Now the Lord of peace himself give you peace always by all means. The Lord be with you all.
verses.context: Closing his second letter to the Thessalonians, Paul prays for the Lord's peace to be with them at all times.

verses.text: Let no man despise thy youth; but be thou an example of the believers, in word, in conversation, in charity, in spirit, in faith, in purity.
verses.displayText: Let no man despise thy youth; but be thou an example of the believers, in word, in conversation, in charity, in spirit, in faith, in purity.
verses.context: Writing to Timothy, a younger coworker facing skepticism because of his age, Paul tells him to lead by example instead.

verses.text: But godliness with contentment is great gain.
verses.displayText: But godliness with contentment is great gain.
verses.context: Warning against teachers who treat religion as a way to get rich, Paul redefines real gain as contentment with what you have.

verses.text: For the love of money is the root of all evil: which while some coveted after, they have erred from the faith, and pierced themselves through with many sorrows.
verses.displayText: For the love of money is the root of all evil: which while some coveted after, they have erred from the faith, and pierced themselves through with many sorrows.
verses.context: Continuing that same warning, Paul identifies the love of money, not money itself, as the root of many troubles.

verses.text: For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.
verses.displayText: For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.
verses.context: Writing to encourage Timothy, Paul reminds him that God gives believers power, love, and self-control, not a spirit of fear.

verses.text: Study to shew thyself approved unto God, a workman that needeth not to be ashamed, rightly dividing the word of truth.
verses.displayText: Study to shew thyself approved unto God, a workman that needeth not to be ashamed, rightly dividing the word of truth.
verses.context: Instructing Timothy on handling his responsibilities well, Paul tells him to work hard at rightly explaining the truth.

verses.text: All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness:
verses.displayText: All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness:
verses.context: Explaining the value of Scripture to Timothy, Paul says it's useful for teaching, correcting, and training people to live well.

verses.text: I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith:
verses.displayText: I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith:
verses.context: Writing near the end of his life, likely awaiting execution, Paul tells Timothy he has fought his fight and stayed faithful to the end.

verses.text: For the word of God is quick, and powerful, and sharper than any twoedged sword, piercing even to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit, and of the joints and marrow, and is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart.
verses.displayText: For the word of God is quick, and powerful, and sharper than any twoedged sword, piercing even to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit, and of the joints and marrow, and is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart.
verses.context: Written to Jewish believers tempted to abandon their faith, this letter describes God's word as sharp enough to reach into a person's deepest thoughts.

verses.text: Let us therefore come boldly unto the throne of grace, that we may obtain mercy, and find grace to help in time of need.
verses.displayText: Let us therefore come boldly unto the throne of grace, that we may obtain mercy, and find grace to help in time of need.
verses.context: Continuing the same argument, the writer encourages believers to approach God's throne boldly rather than fearfully.

verses.text: Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen.
verses.displayText: Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen.
verses.context: Opening a long chapter listing examples of trust from Israel's history, the writer defines what that kind of trust actually is.

verses.text: But without faith it is impossible to please him: for he that cometh to God must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him.
verses.displayText: But without faith it is impossible to please him: for he that cometh to God must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him.
verses.context: Still in the same chapter about historical examples of trust, the writer says pleasing God starts with believing he exists and rewards those who seek him.

verses.text: Looking unto Jesus the author and finisher of our faith; who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising the shame, and is set down at the right hand of the throne of God.
verses.displayText: Looking unto Jesus the author and finisher of our faith; who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising the shame, and is set down at the right hand of the throne of God.
verses.context: Comparing the life of faith to a long-distance race, the writer tells readers to keep their attention on Jesus, who endured the cross for what was ahead of him.

verses.text: Let your conversation be without covetousness; and be content with such things as ye have: for he hath said, I will never leave thee, nor forsake thee.
verses.displayText: Let your conversation be without covetousness; and be content with such things as ye have: for he hath said, I will never leave thee, nor forsake thee.
verses.context: Warning against greed near the end of the letter, the writer reminds readers of a promise that God will never abandon them.

verses.text: Jesus Christ the same yesterday, and to day, and for ever.
verses.displayText: Jesus Christ the same yesterday, and to day, and for ever.
verses.context: This short verse closes a section about steady leaders by describing Jesus himself as never changing over time.

verses.text: If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him.
verses.displayText: If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him.
verses.context: Writing to Jewish believers scattered outside their homeland, James tells them that anyone lacking wisdom can simply ask God for it.

verses.text: But let him ask in faith, nothing wavering. For he that wavereth is like a wave of the sea driven with the wind and tossed.
verses.displayText: But let him ask in faith, nothing wavering. For he that wavereth is like a wave of the sea driven with the wind and tossed.
verses.context: Right after that promise, James adds a condition: ask with genuine trust, not the back-and-forth of someone unsure.

verses.text: Blessed is the man that endureth temptation: for when he is tried, he shall receive the crown of life, which the Lord hath promised to them that love him.
verses.displayText: Blessed is the man that endureth temptation: for when he is tried, he shall receive the crown of life, which the Lord hath promised to them that love him.
verses.context: Encouraging readers going through hard testing, James promises a lasting reward to those who stay faithful through it.

verses.text: Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, and cometh down from the Father of lights, with whom is no variableness, neither shadow of turning.
verses.displayText: Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, and cometh down from the Father of lights, with whom is no variableness, neither shadow of turning.
verses.context: Describing where good things ultimately come from, James calls every good gift a gift that comes down from God, who never changes.

verses.text: Wherefore, my beloved brethren, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath:
verses.displayText: Wherefore, my beloved brethren, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath:
verses.context: Giving practical advice for everyday relationships, James tells his readers to be quick to listen and slow to speak or get angry.

verses.text: Even so faith, if it hath not works, is dead, being alone.
verses.displayText: Even so faith, if it hath not works, is dead, being alone.
verses.context: Arguing that real trust shows up in action, James says trust with no accompanying action is essentially lifeless.

verses.text: Draw nigh to God, and he will draw nigh to you. Cleanse your hands, ye sinners; and purify your hearts, ye double minded.
verses.displayText: Draw nigh to God, and he will draw nigh to you. Cleanse your hands, ye sinners; and purify your hearts, ye double minded.
verses.context: Calling his readers back to sincerity, James tells them that drawing near to God results in God drawing near to them.

verses.text: Confess your faults one to another, and pray one for another, that ye may be healed. The effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much.
verses.displayText: Confess your faults one to another, and pray one for another, that ye may be healed. The effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much.
verses.context: Instructing a community on prayer and honesty, James tells readers to admit their wrongs to each other and pray for one another.

verses.text: But ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people; that ye should shew forth the praises of him who hath called you out of darkness into his marvellous light:
verses.displayText: But ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people; that ye should shew forth the praises of him who hath called you out of darkness into his marvellous light:
verses.context: Writing to Christians scattered across the empire and facing suspicion, Peter tells them they belong to a people specially called out of darkness.

verses.text: But sanctify the Lord God in your hearts: and be ready always to give an answer to every man that asketh you a reason of the hope that is in you with meekness and fear:
verses.displayText: But sanctify the Lord God in your hearts: and be ready always to give an answer to every man that asketh you a reason of the hope that is in you with meekness and fear:
verses.context: Advising Christians facing hostility for their faith, Peter tells them to be ready to explain their hope calmly, without hostility in return.

verses.text: And above all things have fervent charity among yourselves: for charity shall cover the multitude of sins.
verses.displayText: And above all things have fervent charity among yourselves: for charity shall cover the multitude of sins.
verses.context: Near the end of his letter, Peter tells a persecuted church that love toward each other should come before anything else.

verses.text: Humble yourselves therefore under the mighty hand of God, that he may exalt you in due time:
verses.displayText: Humble yourselves therefore under the mighty hand of God, that he may exalt you in due time:
verses.context: Instructing a church under pressure, Peter tells them to humble themselves under God rather than trying to control their own outcome.

verses.text: Casting all your care upon him; for he careth for you.
verses.displayText: Casting all your care upon him; for he careth for you.
verses.context: Right after that instruction, Peter tells readers to hand over their anxiety to God because he genuinely cares about them.

verses.text: Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour:
verses.displayText: Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour:
verses.context: Closing his letter with a warning, Peter compares the devil to a roaring lion looking for someone to attack.

verses.text: The Lord is not slack concerning his promise, as some men count slackness; but is longsuffering to us-ward, not willing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance.
verses.displayText: The Lord is not slack concerning his promise, as some men count slackness; but is longsuffering to us-ward, not willing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance.
verses.context: Responding to people mocking the idea that Jesus would ever return, Peter explains God's delay as patience, giving people time to change.

verses.text: If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
verses.displayText: If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
verses.context: Writing against a teaching that denied the reality of wrongdoing, John tells readers that admitting it leads to being forgiven and made clean.

verses.text: Behold, what manner of love the Father hath bestowed upon us, that we should be called the sons of God: therefore the world knoweth us not, because it knew him not.
verses.displayText: Behold, what manner of love the Father hath bestowed upon us, that we should be called the sons of God: therefore the world knoweth us not, because it knew him not.
verses.context: Marveling at what it means to be part of God's family, John tells his readers to notice the kind of love the Father has given them.

verses.text: Beloved, now are we the sons of God, and it doth not yet appear what we shall be: but we know that, when he shall appear, we shall be like him; for we shall see him as he is.
verses.displayText: Beloved, now are we the sons of God, and it doth not yet appear what we shall be: but we know that, when he shall appear, we shall be like him; for we shall see him as he is.
verses.context: Continuing that same thought, John admits that what believers will eventually become isn't fully clear yet.

verses.text: My little children, let us not love in word, neither in tongue; but in deed and in truth.
verses.displayText: My little children, let us not love in word, neither in tongue; but in deed and in truth.
verses.context: Warning against love that's just talk, John tells his readers that real love shows up in action, not only words.

verses.text: He that loveth not knoweth not God; for God is love.
verses.displayText: He that loveth not knoweth not God; for God is love.
verses.context: Making a direct statement about God's character, John says anyone who doesn't love doesn't actually know God, because God himself is love.

verses.text: There is no fear in love; but perfect love casteth out fear: because fear hath torment. He that feareth is not made perfect in love.
verses.displayText: There is no fear in love; but perfect love casteth out fear: because fear hath torment. He that feareth is not made perfect in love.
verses.context: Continuing to write about love, John says genuine love pushes out fear rather than existing alongside it.

verses.text: We love him, because he first loved us.
verses.displayText: We love him, because he first loved us.
verses.context: Right after that thought, John gives the reason people are even capable of loving: God loved them first.

verses.text: And this is the confidence that we have in him, that, if we ask any thing according to his will, he heareth us:
verses.displayText: And this is the confidence that we have in him, that, if we ask any thing according to his will, he heareth us:
verses.context: Closing his letter with confidence about prayer, John says believers can be sure God hears requests that line up with his will.

verses.text: I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the ending, saith the Lord, which is, and which was, and which is to come, the Almighty.
verses.displayText: I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the ending, saith the Lord, which is, and which was, and which is to come, the Almighty.
verses.context: Opening this vision given to John while exiled on the island of Patmos, the Lord identifies himself as the beginning and the end of everything.

verses.text: Fear none of those things which thou shalt suffer: behold, the devil shall cast some of you into prison, that ye may be tried; and ye shall have tribulation ten days: be thou faithful unto death, and I will give thee a crown of life.
verses.displayText: Fear none of those things which thou shalt suffer: behold, the devil shall cast some of you into prison, that ye may be tried; and ye shall have tribulation ten days: be thou faithful unto death, and I will give thee a crown of life.
verses.context: In a message to a persecuted church in the city of Smyrna, Jesus tells them not to fear coming suffering and promises them life.

verses.text: Behold, I stand at the door, and knock: if any man hear my voice, and open the door, I will come in to him, and will sup with him, and he with me.
verses.displayText: Behold, I stand at the door, and knock: if any man hear my voice, and open the door, I will come in to him, and will sup with him, and he with me.
verses.context: In a message to a self-satisfied church in Laodicea, Jesus pictures himself standing outside, knocking, waiting to be let in.

verses.text: And God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes; and there shall be no more death, neither sorrow, nor crying, neither shall there be any more pain: for the former things are passed away.
verses.displayText: And God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes; and there shall be no more death, neither sorrow, nor crying, neither shall there be any more pain: for the former things are passed away.
verses.context: Describing a vision of a renewed heaven and earth, John writes that God will personally wipe away every tear and end death itself.

verses.text: And he that sat upon the throne said, Behold, I make all things new. And he said unto me, Write: for these words are true and faithful.
verses.displayText: And he that sat upon the throne said, Behold, I make all things new. And he said unto me, Write: for these words are true and faithful.
verses.context: Right after that vision, the one seated on the throne speaks directly, announcing that he is making everything new.

verses.text: Since thou wast precious in my sight, thou hast been honourable, and I have loved thee: therefore will I give men for thee, and people for thy life.
verses.displayText: Since thou wast precious in my sight, thou hast been honourable, and I have loved thee: therefore will I give men for thee, and people for thy life.
verses.context: Speaking to a people facing exile and defeat, Isaiah delivers God's message that they are precious and deeply valued to him.

verses.text: Oh that men would praise the Lord for his goodness, and for his wonderful works to the children of men!
verses.displayText: Oh that men would praise the Lord for his goodness, and for his wonderful works to the children of men!
verses.context: Recalling how God rescued people who cried out to him in distress, this psalm calls on them to actually thank him for it.

verses.text: I sought the Lord, and he heard me, and delivered me from all my fears.
verses.displayText: I sought the Lord, and he heard me, and delivered me from all my fears.
verses.context: Written after David escaped a dangerous situation by pretending to be insane, this verse recalls him seeking God and finding relief from fear.

verses.text: Therefore, my beloved brethren, be ye stedfast, unmoveable, always abounding in the work of the Lord, forasmuch as ye know that your labour is not in vain in the Lord.
verses.displayText: Therefore, my beloved brethren, be ye stedfast, unmoveable, always abounding in the work of the Lord, forasmuch as ye know that your labour is not in vain in the Lord.
verses.context: Closing his long chapter on the resurrection, Paul tells the Corinthians that their efforts for God are never ultimately wasted.
